title: Numerals 7: Money, Age, and Time
description: Apply the 1 / 2-4 / 5+ split to the most common counted nouns: рубль (рубль / рубля / рублей), год (год / года / лет), and час (час / часа / часов).
descriptionRussian: Применяем правило 1 / 2-4 / 5+ к самым частым существительным: рубль (рубль / рубля / рублей), год (год / года / лет) и час (час / часа / часов).
intro: The three things you will actually count out loud. Nothing new in the rule, which is the point: money, age and clock time all run on the same three-way split you already have. There is one irregular form to memorize, and it is the plural of 'year', which is a different word entirely and comes up constantly.
rules: The 1 / 2-4 / 5+ slot is decided by the LAST word of the number: двадцать один рубль (1), двадцать два рубля (2-4), двадцать пять рублей (5+).
Money: один рубль / два рубля / пять рублей. Same pattern for копейка: одна копейка / две копейки / пять копеек.
Age: один год / два года / пять ЛЕТ. The genitive plural of год is the irregular лет, not годов. Age uses the dative person: мне двадцать лет.
Time: один час / два часа / пять часов. The genitive singular часа is stressed on the final -а (два часа).
The teens 11-14 always take the 5+ form, even though they end in 1-4: одиннадцать рублей, двенадцать лет, тринадцать часов.
examples: Это стоит сто рублей. (This costs a hundred roubles.) 100 → 5+ form: рублей.
У меня есть двадцать два рубля. (I have twenty-two roubles.) last word 2 → рубля.
Кофе стоит один рубль. (The coffee costs one rouble.) last word 1 → рубль.
Моему брату двадцать четыре года. (My brother is twenty-four.) last word 4 → года; dative брату.
Бабушке семьдесят лет. (Grandmother is seventy.) 70 → 5+ form: лет; dative бабушке.
Сейчас два часа. (It is two o'clock now.) last word 2 → часа.
Мы ждали пять часов. (We waited five hours.) 5 → часов.
Ему одиннадцать лет. (He is eleven.) 11 → 5+ form: лет, even though it ends in 1.

tables.title: The 1 / 2-4 / 5+ forms for money, age, time

items.hint: 100 falls in the 5+ slot. Which form is that?
items.explanation: Сто (100) belongs to the 5+ group, which takes the genitive plural: сто рублей. Рубля is the 2-4 form; рубль is for numbers ending in 1.

items.hint: Look at the last word: двадцать ДВА.
items.explanation: The last word decides the slot. Двадцать два ends in два (2-4), so the noun is the genitive singular рубля. Рублей is the 5+ form (двадцать пять рублей); рубль follows один.

items.hint: After один the noun stays in the nominative singular.
items.explanation: Numbers ending in один take the nominative singular: один рубль. Only 2-4 (рубля) and 5+ (рублей) change the noun's case.
Двадцать четыре ends in четыре (2-4), so the noun is the genitive singular года: двадцать четыре года. Лет is the 5+ form; год follows один; годов does not exist in modern Russian.

items.hint: 70 is a 5+ number. The genitive plural of год is irregular.
items.explanation: Семьдесят (70) is in the 5+ slot, and the genitive plural of год is the irregular лет (not годов): семьдесят лет. Год follows один and года follows 2-4; age uses the dative person: бабушке.

items.hint: Two o'clock = два + the 2-4 form of час.
items.explanation: Два is in the 2-4 slot, so the noun is the genitive singular часа: два часа. Часов is the 5+ form (пять часов); час follows один.

blanks: Ему одиннадцать _____. (He is eleven years old.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Одиннадцать (11) is a teen, and all teens 11-14 take the 5+ form even though they end in 1-4. The 5+ form for age is the irregular лет: одиннадцать лет. Age uses the dative person: ему.

errorCorrection.sentence: Мы работали одиннадцать часа без перерыва.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We worked eleven hours without a break.
errorCorrection.explanation: The teens 11-14 always count as '5 and up' and take the genitive plural, even though they seem to contain 1-4: одиннадцать часов. Часа is the genitive singular, the trap a learner falls into by hearing 'один' inside одиннадцать.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: My sister is twenty-two years old.
errorCorrection.explanation: The irregular form лет is the genitive PLURAL of год, used only after 5 and up (пять лет). This number ends in два, so it follows the 2-4 rule and needs the genitive singular года: двадцать два года. Лет is a real and very common form, just wrong here, which makes it the classic over-correction once a learner has met пять лет. Год is the bare nominative (after один: двадцать один год), and годов does not exist in modern Russian. Age is given with the dative person: моей сестре.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The shop has been closed for six hours already.
errorCorrection.explanation: After 5 and up the noun goes into the genitive plural: шесть часов. Часа is the genitive singular, correct after 2-4 (два часа, with the stress on the final -а) but not after шесть. Час is the bare nominative (один час). The split for час is exactly the same as for any noun: один час, два часа, пять часов.

minimalPairs.explanation: The last word decides the slot. Двадцать один ends in один, so the noun is the nominative singular год: двадцать один год. Лет (5+) would be wrong here; that is for numbers like двадцать пять.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The shop is open until five o'clock.
minimalPairs.explanation: Пять is in the 5+ slot, so the noun is the genitive plural часов: до пяти часов. Часа is the 2-4 form (два часа). Note that до also calls for the genitive, which the 5+ form already supplies.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each number by which form of год it takes for age.

reviewVocab.definition: rouble in the three counting slots: один рубль (1), два рубля (2-4), пять рублей (5+).
year for age: один год, два года, but irregular пять ЛЕТ in the 5+ slot. Age uses the dative person.
hour and clock time: один час, два часа, пять часов. The genitive singular часа is end-stressed.
